analysis:
Examined Messages.swift in two places. The base side, lines 1718-2066, covers the CoordinatorMessage structs and their Codable implementation. The head side, lines 1-648, covers the prefix-cache status types, Register, Heartbeat, InferenceError and the PrefixCache lookup/ready structs.

The security-relevant change adds an optional `busy: ProviderBusy?` field to Register (head 248-251, 281-282, 286) and to Heartbeat (head 344-346, 363-364, 366). The field is provider-authored, advisory and only reduces routing: it marks the provider draining or excluded while an add-on hold refuses work. A malicious provider (ADV-001) could already refuse work or report a draining status, so the field adds no trust escalation. It carries no prompt data (A-001) and has no authorization, attestation or billing effect visible here.

Other head ranges (948-951, 1070, 1097, 1345-1346, 1371-1372) are presumably the encode/decode additions for `busy`. They were not visible in these units, so the encoding of the busy fields (busy_reason, busy_since_ms, busy_addon) and the ProviderBusy definition were not reviewed.

Integration should confirm the following:
- The busy addon/reason strings are bounded and do not carry request-derived or identifying data (T-058 diagnostics leak class).
- The coordinator treats `busy` only as a routing exclusion and never as a capacity or trust grant.
- No inference request is accepted and then dropped while busy without a terminal error (T-010 availability).

The base CoordinatorMessage decoding is unchanged in this diff. Cache fields related to T-041 are unchanged. No regression was identified in the reviewed text.
